name: Jerry Seinfeld
premise: A sane man filing compliance reports on an insane species from a safe distance.

bits.text: How are you. Good, how are you. That's the whole program, and I don't think anybody's read the source code. I tested it once, told the guy at the bodega my back was killing me. He just asked again. He wasn't listening, he was rebooting. We're two machines exchanging a handshake packet that says nothing and confirming the connection is fine.

bits.text: Nobody has ever once answered "How are you?" honestly. You can't. The protocol won't allow it. You say "good, you?" and they say "good," and what we've just completed is four words to confirm two people are willing to keep existing. That's the entire transaction.

bits.text: We're all running the same program. "How are you?" "Good. How are you?" That's not a conversation, that's two servers pinging each other to prove they're still online. Nobody has answered that question once in human history! You know what the first honest answer to "how are you?" would be? Nobody's ever gotten it, and the second you give it, the friendship is over. We are beggars trading fake money!
